title: Grouping & counting
learn: keys that describe a group (sorted string, count tuple), frequency maps, set-based sequence tricks
hook: Group Anagrams, Top K Frequent and Longest Consecutive Sequence are all on the NeetCode 150 and Grind 75 lists. They look different, but each one is "choose the right key for a dict or set".

explain.prompt: Explain how you'd group anagrams and why your approach is faster than comparing every pair of words.
keyPoints: anagrams share a canonical key: the sorted word or a tuple of 26 letter counts
a dict from key to list collects each group in one pass
O(n · k log k) with sorted keys, O(n · k) with count keys, vs O(n² · k) comparing pairs
keys must be hashable, so counts go in a tuple, not a list
